answer: Time-Locked Reputation Decay: Each agent identity accrues reputation only through sustained useful output, and that reputation decays on a fixed clock; cloning resets it to zero. Enforcement: new identities carry no history, so they cannot bid on high-value tasks until the clock elapses. An attacker cloning N agents pays N× the elapsed wall-clock time plus N× compute to reach parity, while honest agents keep accrued value. A hollow clone has no pulse of activity and must wander for weeks before matching one established peer.
